analysis.title: US TMT Quick Hits - 3 Nov 2026 (Peter Callahan)
key_insights: NDX is +60 bps on 3 Nov, led by Semis up about 2.5%, after October weighed on risk appetite. Earnings tonight are the focus, especially AMD and ANET.
The GS TMT trading desk (Pete Bartlett) reports a more balanced flow picture today, versus few signs of defense over the last few days.

Callahan lists four narrative 'boxes' at least partially checked: earnings, financing, Oil/Rates relief (for now), and positioning and valuation resets. He says it still feels hard to string together more than a few good days.
The US mid-term election is tonight. Per the GS Econ preview, GIR expects the focus on Democrats to fade somewhat after the election.
Top client inbounds: why Semis are strong (CRDO, MPWR, TTMI, APH), Apple's path from here, RBLX/RDDT/APP up 5-7%, bogeys on AMD and DDOG, and weakness in DASH and online travel agencies.

Earnings tonight: ALAB, AMD, ANET, ANGI, BKNG, CPNG, DUOL, FLYW, FRSH, HURN, NVTS, OUST, PCOR, RVLV, SWKS, TOST, TREE, TRVG, XYZ. Most asked on AMD 4Q guide expectations, ANET CY27 framing, and BKNG 4Q guidance.

Software, especially 'inference economy' names: the bar is high. If growth is not accelerating in 3Q and into 4Q, the stocks are not rising. This showed in NOW, FTNT, TWLO, PLTR, CHKP and DT. Focus shifts next to DDOG, NET, RBRK and OKTA.
Market is applying lower multiples to 2028 estimates in Semis and AI infra because of perceived lack of visibility. Several 2028 datapoints could help the AI trade when risk appetite improves.

2028 datapoints: AMZN guided to 2027/2028 AWS growth. TSM did not raise its long-term AI accelerator revenue CAGR but said demand is extremely robust with no sign of slowdown. Samsung said memory supply tightness will last through 2027 and into 2028.

More 2028 datapoints: SPCX said compute pricing is tracking slightly above the high end of the $30-$50 per watt range. AEIS said Semis and DC customers project demand strengthening through 2027 into 2028. STX said most nearline exabyte supply is allocated under LTSAs through C'28.

Analog Semis (TXN, NXPI, MPWR, ON) have had choppy price action, but results and price action feel 'glass half full' relative to other Semis pockets. Yesterday's ISM Manufacturing print was better than expected. IFX, STM and MCHP report in coming days.

Internet is split. GenAI is emerging as a tailwind to e-commerce growth (personalization, cataloging, listings) per ETSY, EBAY and CVNA. Advertising is choppy (PINS cited EU headwinds), and RDDT flagged search referral traffic changes from shifting AI workflows.

Services show signs of pressure. IT fell 13% as ex-US federal contract value grew just 2.8% y/y, and Gartner no longer expects to reach its prior 4% year-end target (per GIR). CTSH guided lighter on 4Q on weaker discretionary spending in Healthcare and Consumer. INFY cut guidance on sluggish demand and shifting client spend priorities.

Consumer: V and MA both reported better-than-expected results. October payment volume is tracking better than expected quarter-to-date despite step-downs from a strong September, with no notable weakness across consumer bands.
Chart of the day: Info Tech and Communication Services accounted for more than 60% of S&P 500 Q3 EPS growth, yet sit at the bottom of the table for T+1 earnings returns.

tension_points.bull_case: Plenty of 2028 visibility datapoints (AMZN, TSM, Samsung, SPCX, AEIS, STX) could help the AI trade when risk appetite improves. Narrative boxes are partly checked: earnings, financing, Oil/Rates relief, positioning and valuation resets.
tension_points.bear_case: Price action has been tough, the market applies lower multiples to 2028 estimates, and it is hard to string together more than a few good days. Info Tech and Comm Services sit at the bottom of the T+1 returns table despite driving over 60% of Q3 EPS growth.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Growth failing to accelerate in 3Q and into 4Q for software and inference economy names, as seen in recent earnings reactions.
